deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a magnetometer reading series from Gauss's (Göttingen, Gauss–Weber) induction experiments. Run 'I b' was taken with the bar magnet 'Pol oben' (pole up). The previous page has the companion runs 'V' and 'I … Pol unten'.

Data. There are 12 successive turning points (elongations) a_0..a_11 of the needle, in scale divisions:
604.8, 1251.4, 743.1, 1114.9, 876.8, 982.3, 1006.4, 852.7, 1133.0, 726.0, 1257.9, 601.8.
The amplitude |a_{i+1}-a_i| runs 646.6, 508.3, 371.8, 238.1, 105.5, 24.1, 153.7, 280.3, 407.0, 531.9, 656.1. It falls by an almost constant ~130 per half-swing, passes through zero and grows again. A constant ~130-step (rather than a geometric decay) is the signature of a force whose direction is reversed at every half-swing, as with a commutated induction current (Weber's multiplication/recoil technique). The equilibrium point therefore alternates between two values, c1 and c2.

Column 1. For the pairs (a_0,a_1), (a_2,a_3), …, (a_10,a_11) Gauss writes the sum and the difference:
- 1856.2 + 646.6
- 1858.0 + 371.8
- 1859.1 + 105.5
- 1859.1 − 153.7
- 1859.0 − 407.0
- 1859.7 − 656.1

Column 3. For the pairs (a_1,a_2), (a_3,a_4), …, (a_9,a_10):
- 1994.5 − 508.3
- 1991.7 − 238.1
- 1988.7 + 24.1
- 1985.7 + 280.3
- 1983.9 + 531.9

Each sum s ≈ 2c (twice a rest position). The two families give 2c1 ≈ 1858.5 and 2c2 ≈ 1988.9.

Damping model. Because of damping, s depends slightly and linearly on the swing d = a_{i+1} − a_i. Gauss posits s = S − x·d with an unknown small coefficient x. Averaging gives:
- S1 = mean(s) + x·mean(d) = 11151.1/6 + x·(−92.9/6) = 1858.517 − 15.5x
- S2 = 9944.5/5 + x·(89.9/5) = 1988.900 + 18.0x
- Difference: S2 − S1 = 130.383 + 33.5x

Determining x (right-hand block). x is fixed from the end-to-end drift of the sums against the end-to-end change of d.
- Family 1: the sums rise 1856.2 → 1859.7, i.e. by 3.5, while d changes by 646.6 + 656.1 = 1302.7.
- Family 3: the sums fall 1994.5 → 1983.9, i.e. by 10.6, while d changes by 508.3 + 531.9 = 1040.2.
- Pooling: 14.1 against 2342.9, so 1/x = 2342.9/14.1 = 166.2, i.e. x ≈ 0.00602.

Correction. The term 33.5x = 33.5/166.2 = 0.202; this is the '202' written under the difference line. The final corrected value is not written on the page; my completion is S2 − S1 = 130.383 + 0.202 = 130.585. That means the two alternating rest positions differ by ≈ 65.29 divisions, a deflection of ≈ ±32.65 about their mean. This quantity is compared with the 'V' run (128.989) and the 'Pol unten' run (125.457 + 172.2x) on the previous page.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. All sums, differences, means (1858.517, 1988.900, −15.48→−15.5, 17.98→18.0), the difference 130.383, the drifts 3.5 and 10.6, the totals 1302.7, 1040.2 and 2342.9, the ratio 166.2 and the correction 0.202 check.

Methodological remark, not an error: x is estimated crudely from endpoint drifts (pooled ratio 14.1/2342.9) rather than by a least-squares fit of s on d. Separately, the two families give rather different x (1/372 vs 1/98), which shows the linear damping model fits only roughly. The effect on the result is only ~0.2 divisions.

results.what: Rest position from sums of consecutive turning points, s = a_i + a_{i+1} ≈ 2c, with a linear damping correction s = S − x·d determined from the data
results.modern_name: Estimation of the equilibrium of a damped oscillator from turning points (linear correction for logarithmic decrement)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard Gauss/Weber magnetometer practice of the 1830s (Göttingen Magnetic Union)

results.what: Measurement of a deflection via current reversal at each half-swing: amplitude changes linearly by ~2×deflection per half-period and the rest point alternates between two values
results.modern_name: Multiplication / recoil method (Multiplikations- bzw. Zurückwerfungsmethode) for ballistic galvanometer / induction measurements
results.usually_credited_to: W. Weber and C. F. Gauss (late 1830s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine experimental data reduction in the Gauss–Weber induction and magnetometer programme, using methods already published and associated with Gauss and Weber. It is of documentary interest only.

checkable.asserts: corrected difference ≈130.585 (not written on the page)

transcription_corrections: Reading 3 is 1114.9, not 1104.9. The sum 1858.0 = 743.1 + 1114.9 and the differences 371.8 and −238.1 require it.
'202' is the correction 33.5/166.2 = 0.202 written under the difference line, not an independent number.
The right-hand block reads: 3.5 | 1302.7 / 10.6 | 1040.2 / 14.1 | 2342.9 / 166.2 (ratio). These are drifts of the sums against total amplitude changes.
